title: De-AI Your UI: 5 Dashboard Fixes
summary: This lesson identifies common 'tells' of AI-generated UI designs and provides five specific fixes to make dashboards look more professional. It covers gradients, icon tiles, hierarchy, shadows, and copy refinement.

transcript.text: Your dashboard looks AI-made. 5 tells, 5 fixes.
Tell 1: The gradient. Purple to blue on the header, the button, the chart fill. A generated UI paints gradients where it has nothing to say. One flat accent. Now color means something.
Tell 2: Icons in pastel tiles. Blue, green, purple, orange, one per card. Four colors for four numbers is decoration, not information. Drop the tiles. The number is the hero.

Tell 3: Hierarchy. Four identical cards, same size, same weight, same green badge. A dashboard with no hierarchy is a spreadsheet with padding. One primary metric, big. Three secondary, small. Your eye lands once.

Tell 4: Shadows. 16 pixel corners and a drop shadow on everything. Cards, inputs, badges, the chart. When every card floats, nothing does. Hairline borders, tighter radius on smaller parts, shadow only on what opens above the page.
Tell 5: Copy. Welcome back, Jordan, waving hand. +12.5% from last month. Placeholder copy and numbers with no shape. Name the period. Tabular digits. A sparkline instead of a badge.
5 tells gone. Or type /restyle. UX Engine, the Claude code plugin that kills the AI look. Link in bio.

before_after: A generic, AI-generated dashboard with excessive gradients and shadows is transformed into a professional interface with clear hierarchy, flat accents, and precise data visualization.
